gone off = no longer safe or pleasant to eat because it is too old
use-by date = the last date a perishable food should be eaten for safety
best-before date = the date until which a food is at its best quality
shelf life = how long a food stays good to eat under proper storage
food poisoning = an illness caused by eating contaminated food
contamination = the presence of harmful bacteria or substances in food
cross-contamination = the spread of harmful bacteria from one food or surface to another
simmer = to cook just below boiling point, with small bubbles
roast = to cook food in an oven with fat, often meat or vegetables
ferment = to change food through the action of yeast or bacteria
sauté = to fry quickly in a small amount of fat
stew = to cook slowly in liquid; a dish cooked that way
braise = to fry food briefly and then cook it slowly in a little liquid
poach = to cook gently in water or another liquid that is not quite boiling
blanch = to put food briefly into boiling water, then often into cold water
pickle = to preserve food in vinegar or salt water
cure = to preserve meat or fish with salt, smoke or both
marinate = to leave food in a flavoured liquid so it absorbs taste
knead = to press and fold dough with your hands
whisk = to beat eggs or cream quickly until light
